No, not all prime numbers are even. A prime number is defined as a natural number greater than 1 that has no positive divisors other than 1 and itself. Here are some examples of prime numbers:

- 2 (the smallest prime number)
- 3
- 5
- 7
- 11
- 13
- 17

You can see that the only even prime number is 2. All other prime numbers are odd, as they cannot be divided evenly by 2 without leaving a remainder.
